topics.name: Medical vision-language diagnosis
topics.summary: Across chest X-ray adaptation, slit-lamp disease classification, and grounding tests, the methods combine image evidence with clinical context and explicitly probe whether visual signals drive predictions. Results emphasize cross-site robustness, subtype discrimination, and more reliable multimodal diagnosis.

topics.name: Clinical generative AI and decision support
topics.summary: The papers evaluate language models for pharmacovigilance and diabetes care, and add patient-conditioned graph reasoning for traditional prescriptions. Expert or audit-oriented assessments show that useful clinical assistance depends on evidence, personalization, and safety-aware scoring rather than fluent text alone.

topics.name: Multimodal clinical imaging and computational pathology
topics.summary: These studies build clinical image resources and models spanning scanned records, adaptive low-dose CT acquisition, PET/CT and OCT diagnosis, and paired uterine slides with reports. They use multimodal fusion, structure-aware sampling, and expert validation to improve reconstruction, detection, and report-oriented research.

topics.name: Continual medical image AI
topics.summary: Sequential virtual staining and radiology reporting systems preserve clinically meaningful relations as domains or tasks change. Distillation, multi-agent generation, and region-grounded checking reduce forgetting and help keep generated findings tied to image evidence.

topics.name: Auditable and equitable clinical screening
topics.summary: Screening studies examine explanation quality, calibration, synthetic-noise robustness, and subgroup-specific misses in child-trauma and chest X-ray settings. Their results show that operating thresholds and tail behavior can change clinical conclusions even when aggregate accuracy looks strong.

topics.name: Speech recognition, synthesis, and paralinguistic processing
topics.summary: The papers improve speech systems through quality-aware sampling, timestamp repair, affective timing, accent tokenization, embedding analysis, and pseudo-speaker generation. Across recognition and voice transformation tasks, better supervision and identity control support out-of-domain accuracy, intelligibility, privacy, and emotional expressiveness.

topics.name: Sign language and myoelectric gesture recognition
topics.summary: Visual pose cues support gloss-free sign translation, while adversarial and metric learning make EMG gesture embeddings less dependent on the wearer. Both use complementary nonverbal signals to improve recognition when subjects or conditions change.

topics.name: Multimodal human state monitoring
topics.summary: Egocentric video, inertial and gaze streams, sleep physiology, and flight-session biosignals are modeled as time-aligned evidence of movement, workload, impairment, or fatigue. Benchmarks and physiology-aware fusion reveal benefits from temporal synchronization, multimodal context, and resilience to missing signals.

topics.name: Efficient neural inference and transformer compression
topics.summary: Hardware-aware attention, pruning, low-bit computation, compact language-model adaptation, speculative decoding, and sparse context selection reduce inference cost. Evaluations span FPGA and XR accelerators, vision Transformers, tiny language models, and long-context decoding while tracking accuracy, latency, memory, and energy.

topics.name: Cybersecurity threat detection and platform defense
topics.summary: Malware-image classification, vulnerability topic mining, IDE jailbreaks, and malicious-link studies expose different attack surfaces. Hybrid visual features, language-model clustering, and workflow-level analysis indicate that defenses must cover artifacts and multi-step propagation, not just isolated messages.

topics.name: Transportation optimization and control
topics.summary: Capacity planning from business text, collaborative route construction, traffic-signal reinforcement learning, and prediction-assisted tours address distinct transportation decisions. The recurring tools are structured optimization, feasibility-preserving coordination, interpretable control, and guarantees or safety constraints for deployment.

topics.name: Verified engineering automation
topics.summary: Access-policy synthesis, analog-circuit optimization, and netlist-to-schematic conversion use constrained interfaces, verifier feedback, and machine-checkable intermediate artifacts. Their shared result is more dependable engineering automation because proposed actions and generated designs can be checked before release.

topics.name: Agent self-improvement and verified orchestration
topics.summary: Coding-harness changes, retry feedback, self-optimizing memory, skill production, solver-verified reasoning, reward-gated distillation, and evolutionary exploration all turn agent experience into later improvements. The studies favor targeted feedback, admissible revisions, and evaluation of both model behavior and the surrounding execution process.

topics.name: Multi-agent collaboration and proactive coordination
topics.summary: Network analyses of language agents, breakdown-aware collaboration, and enterprise context graphs examine when agents should share information or act ahead of a user request. Influence modeling, state-change detection, and selective interventions aim to improve coordination while limiting distraction and herding.

topics.name: Robot manipulation and visuomotor control
topics.summary: VLA routing, tactile residual adaptation, search-distilled action scoring, adversarial planning, diffusion policies, 3D world-action models, mixture-of-experts control, and object-persistence prediction address manipulation under uncertainty. Results emphasize transfer across sensors, dynamics, scenes, and long-horizon consequences.

topics.name: Controllable generative media
topics.summary: Conversational asset authoring for virtual reality and proxy-conditioned video synthesis make generative media respond to user intent or desired motion. One couples elicitation with concept confirmation; the other transfers dynamics from unpaired proxy clips without requiring target-video pairs.

topics.name: Multimodal reasoning and generation
topics.summary: Token-level attention analysis, interleaved text-image decision processes, emergent-language reconstruction, and tri-modal audio-video question answering study how models combine modalities. The methods use intervention, diffusion reconstruction, or parallel fusion to improve evidence use and robustness across visual and acoustic tasks.

topics.name: Earth observation vision and remote sensing
topics.summary: Remote-sensing studies cover forest biomass estimation, UAV target segmentation, onboard lightweight models, referring segmentation, traffic-object datasets, and pixel-wise Earth foundation models. Optical, radar, foundation-model, and spatial-program cues improve performance under clouds, scarce labels, scale variation, and edge-compute limits.

topics.name: 3D reconstruction and Gaussian scene modeling
topics.summary: Indoor component semantics, sparse-view surfaces, city-scale geometry, articulated objects, blurred or close-up views, and single-panorama generation are handled with multimodal labels, depth and normal priors, Gaussian splats, completion, and canonical constraints. The recurring goal is detailed, scalable geometry from incomplete imagery.

topics.name: Geometric computer vision and representation learning
topics.summary: Geometry-grounded tracking, dense occupancy routing, order-equivariant graph and sheaf networks, and deterministic consensus estimation use explicit structure to stabilize visual or relational inference. Across benchmarks, geometric constraints replace some dependence on appearance, random sampling, or fixed message-passing assumptions.

topics.name: Theoretical foundations of neural representations
topics.summary: Theoretical analyses connect activation thresholds, thin-layer PINN bases, polytope depth, lottery-ticket structure, and gradient-flow estimation to expressivity or optimization. They combine proofs with controlled experiments to explain when compact nonlinear representations preserve accuracy or capture difficult geometry.

topics.name: Robust ML evaluation under distribution shift
topics.summary: Validation geometry can distort data-value scores, text detectors can fail across generators and domains, and diffusion classifiers expose shortcut and minority-region biases. Together the evaluations argue for shift-aware baselines, explicit failure taxonomies, and reporting beyond a single clean accuracy number.

topics.name: Efficient generative modeling
topics.summary: Few-step discrete diffusion, on-device video diffusion, flow-mixture inference, conditional image synthesis, preference-distilled video, and latent-backbone refinement all reduce generation cost or artifacts. Their experiments balance sampling speed, posterior coverage, fidelity, and robustness across image, video, and probabilistic modeling tasks.

topics.name: Multimodal embodied navigation
topics.summary: Indoor navigation papers move beyond waypoint success by checking instance-level targets, recognizing stairs with multiple signals, and benchmarking long-horizon audio-visual-language missions. Object grounding, hazard-aware exploration, and persistent mission context improve search and recovery in constrained environments.

topics.name: Robust sensor fusion and navigation estimation
topics.summary: Aided inertial navigation analysis characterizes when unknown sensor delays are identifiable, while infrared detection and surface-vehicle perception learn to weight unreliable or asynchronous modalities. The common emphasis is on calibration, quality-aware fusion, and reliable situational awareness under changing sensing conditions.

topics.name: Test-time adaptation under distribution drift
topics.summary: Source-free deployment methods update prompts or lightweight model components using self-ensembles, foundation-model proposals, and regulated interaction. They target unlabeled shifts while limiting compute, instability, and forgetting, and frame adaptation as a controlled response to nonstationary observations.

topics.name: Language model uncertainty and early failure detection
topics.summary: Long-form generation, natural-language risk statements, task-oriented dialogue, and Text-to-SQL trajectories are used to test confidence and failure signals. Deterministic labels, hidden-state probes, belief-state changes, and execution consistency help identify unreliable outputs before they reach an expensive or user-facing step.

topics.name: AI-generated image forensics
topics.summary: Cross-paradigm texture relations and semantic-geometric consistency between facial regions provide complementary evidence for detecting synthetic imagery. Cross-dataset tests emphasize transfer across generators and resilience to manipulations that remove obvious pixel artifacts.

topics.name: Trustworthy language-agent systems
topics.summary: Personal-agent prompt-injection defenses, latent Text-to-SQL vulnerability discovery, and neuro-symbolic critical-scenario attribution make agent behavior more inspectable. They combine taint-aware safeguards, automated probing, structured evidence, and symbolic operations to expose risks that ordinary answer scores miss.

topics.name: Secure and structured retrieval for language models
topics.summary: RAG systems are tested or improved with poisoning benchmarks, metadata filters, candidate-constrained generation, claim-source verification, and adaptive graph construction. The recurring design is selective evidence access plus explicit checks, improving resistance to hijacking while preserving recall, fidelity, and low-cost reasoning.

topics.name: Evidence-guided visual reasoning
topics.summary: Industrial anomaly detection and Bengali meme explanation organize visual, textual, and contextual evidence before making a decision. Reference comparisons, local search, OCR, and evidence-sentence annotations make predictions more traceable than similarity-only matching and support evaluation in specialized or low-resource settings.

topics.name: Adaptive EEG decoding
topics.summary: Imagined-speech decoding and EEG foundation-model adaptation combine temporal neural encoders with subject- or task-aware updates. Spiking dynamics, cross-view alignment, and online feature modulation are used to retain performance as users and recording conditions vary.

topics.name: Sponsored search and generative recommendation
topics.summary: E-commerce systems use inventory-aware query generation, language-model relevance scoring, semantic item codes, and time-gap tokens to model changing intent. Experiments on search and Amazon-style interaction data seek better coverage, ranking, and preference tracking without giving up serving efficiency.

topics.name: Robust learning under data corruption
topics.summary: Medical classifiers, sparse feature selectors, and training-free image denoisers are evaluated when inputs or supports are unreliable. Natural corruption tests, adversarial stability objectives, and fixed local restoration operators show complementary routes to dependable predictions without assuming clean or in-domain data.

topics.name: Selective and continual language-model adaptation
topics.summary: Concept suppression and recursive low-rank consolidation address the tension between changing a language model and retaining prior abilities. Prompt-condition selection, spectrum-aware updates, and worst-case retention tests focus adaptation on needed behavior while reducing interference across tasks.

topics.name: Representation steering and interpretability
topics.summary: Dialect control, concept erasure, semantic projection steering, and temporal-graph attribution modify or explain internal representations. Sparse directions, manifold constraints, memory backtracking, and contribution accounting aim to improve controllability while making the sources of model behavior more visible.

topics.name: Robot planning under dynamics and uncertainty
topics.summary: Kinodynamic search, model-predictive path-integral control, and finite-reliability belief-space covers are studied with computational or stability guarantees. Vectorized sampling, finite-sample analysis, and bounded-loss abstractions connect fast planning with explicit handling of noise and imperfect actuation.

topics.name: Causal and dependency-aware statistical learning
topics.summary: Order-based causal discovery, treatment-effect splitting, targeted HAL estimation, and scalable conditional-dependency mining address structure and function estimation under high-dimensional data. They combine honest or regularized estimation with pruning, parallel search, and uncertainty-aware inference.

topics.name: Optimizer design and inverse optimization
topics.summary: Learning-rate safeguards and optimizer taxonomies analyze curvature, tuning, memory, and training cost, while a neural forward model supports gradient-based inverse design of thermal sensors. Together they treat optimization as both a training-control problem and a constrained engineering decision.

topics.name: Representation learning and encoder design
topics.summary: Controlled studies compare glyph images with token embeddings, separate reconstruction from semantic representation, and test Siamese student encoders in JEPA training. The results link input form, objective design, and encoder sharing to separability, scaling, and convergence.

topics.name: Online optimization for resource-constrained operations
topics.summary: Model-serving and order-fulfillment decisions are decomposed or priced with dual variables, future-cost estimates, and value feedback. These methods coordinate capacity, latency, routing, and synchronization constraints more effectively than independent heuristics while keeping decisions interpretable.

topics.name: Formalized statistical analysis and evaluation
topics.summary: Proof-oriented Python analysis and an algebraic metric framework make statistical assumptions and classification scores easier to audit. Shared formal operators, executable transformations, and consistent aggregation reduce ambiguity across hypothesis testing, meta-analysis, and performance reporting.

topics.name: Prediction with incomplete or scarce data
topics.summary: Genomic survival models handle missing heterogeneous features, while synthetic-tabular benchmarks and agricultural augmentation examine fidelity and downstream utility; crowd-state experiments compare tabular foundation models with tuned conventional learners. The studies map when extra data, model capacity, or labels actually improve prediction.

topics.name: Human-centered governance and evaluation of AI agents
topics.summary: Agent benchmarks, coding-agent scholarship, interaction-readiness frameworks, and governed local runtimes examine role boundaries, user control, permissioned tools, and reproducible evaluation. They argue that useful agents need human-facing accountability and operational safeguards in addition to task success.

topics.name: Operational assurance for deployed AI
topics.summary: Monitoring services and medical-device reporting analyses connect calibration, drift, fairness, uncertainty, and lifecycle evidence to deployment claims. The recurring message is that audit-ready operations must expose limitations and ongoing performance, not rely on regulatory clearance or offline benchmarks alone.

topics.name: Memory mechanisms for continual reinforcement learning
topics.summary: Navigation replay and sensitivity-weighted value updates preserve useful experience across changing scenes or sequential learning stages. Both methods adapt target construction or memory organization to reduce catastrophic forgetting while maintaining stability and transfer.

topics.name: Multilingual grammar and machine translation
topics.summary: A Korean corpus annotation scheme distinguishes adnominal constructions beyond surface morphology, while a medieval Latin study compares simpler translation pipelines. Both show that language-specific structure and reproducible annotation or evaluation choices materially affect downstream NLP conclusions.

topics.name: Computational biology and molecular discovery
topics.summary: Diffusion-based inverse modeling, an open all-atom co-folding engine, codon-harmonization optimization, and methylation trajectory inference apply generative or structured learning to biological systems. They model latent dynamics, sequence design, molecular interactions, or aging trajectories from simulated and cross-sectional data.

topics.name: Physics-informed scientific machine learning
topics.summary: Spectral features with learnable metrics, neural instance segmentation of detonation foils, physics-aware Transformers for pulsar timing, and local linear neural operators embed domain structure into learning. Evaluations on physical simulations and experiments report better efficiency, robustness, or parameter inference than generic baselines.

topics.name: AI-assisted scientific scholarship
topics.summary: Graph-based survey planning, reflections on agentic discovery, and critiques of generative scholarship examine how AI changes literature synthesis, conjecture formation, and scholarly judgment. The papers emphasize citation structure, human expertise, and the risks of delegating formative research practices.

topics.name: Educational technology and curriculum analytics
topics.summary: Mixed-reality and tangible post-lecture environments are compared with conventional instruction, while portfolio-scale curriculum analysis matches learning outcomes to job-market competencies. The studies combine controlled learning measures with reproducible labor-market evidence to identify modality benefits and systemic skill gaps.

topics.name: Relational and federated machine learning
topics.summary: A controlled relational-database benchmark standardizes tasks across tables and model families, while federated Transformer training reallocates update magnitude according to coordinate reliability under client heterogeneity. Both show why fair comparisons and data-aware optimization matter when structure or distribution differs across sources.

topics.name: Function calling reliability
topics.summary: Replication across language models measures how natural-language tool interfaces affect parsing, token use, and task success, while a calibrated abstention filter blocks low-confidence calls. Together they treat tool reliability as a combination of interface design, model behavior, and selective refusal.
